subject: Proposal: graduated SLA uplift + seat-discount scenarios
messages:
From: Tom Miller <tom.m@brightgrid.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@brightgrid.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA uplift & seat discount — initial ask

Jordan — thanks for the call this morning. We had two follow-ups from the product and finance teams: 1) can you show examples of how the uplifted SLA (99.95% -> 99.99%) changes monthly run-rate for our expected token volumes, and 2) how would a seat-based discount ladder interact with a committed spend?

High level: BrightGrid is evaluating an initial 50-seat rollout across API Producers with ~250M tokens/mo. We need clear options (pilot / 12mo / 24mo) and the associated crediting for SLA misses. Attached is a simple worksheet (bg_usage_estimate.csv) that shows our traffic pattern.

Can you confirm whether escalation coverage (on-call contact, severity 1 24x7) is included in the Plus tier or treated as an add-on?

Thanks —
Tom
Head of Platform
BrightGrid

Attachment: bg_usage_estimate.csv (csv stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Miller <tom.m@brightgrid.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@brightgrid.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uplift & seat discount — initial ask

Tom — appreciate the details and the worksheet. Quick answers up front: 1) escalation coverage is configurable — Plus includes business-hours triage and a 24x7 escalation path for Severity 1 as an add-on or bundled at Enterprise; 2) seat discounts can be structured as a ladder tied to committed spend or per-seat volume thresholds.

I'll put together three concrete options (Pilot, Plus 12mo, Enterprise 24mo) with modeled TCV and monthly run-rate impact. Sending a formal sheet in a follow-up.

Couple requests from my side so the model is accurate:
- Confirm tokens/mo cadence (are 250M tokens steady or seasonal peaks?)
- Are you aiming to lock a maximum spend per month or allow burst overage?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla_pricing_v1.xlsx (xlsx stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Tom Miller <tom.m@brightgrid.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@brightgrid.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift & seat discount — proposal packet

Tom / Sara — attached is the proposal packet (sla_uplift_options.pdf) with three options and worked examples. Summary below: 

Option A — Pilot (3 months)
- Uptime: 99.95%
- Response: 4hr business-hours for Severity 1
- Escalation: on-call pager during business hours
- Seat discount: none; standard per-seat pricing
- Use case: evaluate performance and prefix caching benefits

Option B — Plus (12 months) — recommended for initial production
- Uptime: 99.975%
- Response: 1hr business-hours; 24x7 escalation for S1 as add-on ($5k/mo)
- Seat discount: 10% at 50 seats, increases to 13% at 100 seats
- SLA credits: pro-rated token-based credit for downtime > SLA threshold, capped at 30% of monthly bill

Option C — Enterprise (24 months)
- Uptime: 99.99%
- Response: 30min 24x7 for S1; named on-call rotation + quarterly runbooks
- Seat discount: 15% at 50 seats; 20% at 100+ seats; 24% with 24mo commit
- Additional: nested escalation, white-glove onboarding, extended log retention

Examples in the packet show net monthly run-rate change for your 250M tokens scenario and three seat tiers. Key notes:
- Seat discounts shown are mutually exclusive with consumption commit discounts; we can blend on request but it reduces margin predictability.
- Escalation add-on pricing is shown as a fixed monthly fee in Plus, included in Enterprise.
- SLA crediting formula uses token-weighted minutes below target (see section 4).

Next steps suggested: 1) pick a preferred option, 2) SalesOps will run a TCV model, 3) legal will provide a targeted amendment with the SLA clause and crediting table.

Link: HubSpot deal — https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4721

Jordan

Attachment: sla_uplift_options.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.m@brightgrid.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: BrightGrid — pricing anchor and concession guardrails

Jordan / Aditya — adding a few internal guardrails before we present a final number to Tom: 
- Recommend we anchor on Plus as the commercial closure: it balances SLA uplift vs. add-on pricing and minimizes unknowns.
- Seat-based discounts should be tiered by committed seats, not just listed seat count; otherwise we lose renewal leverage.
- If Sales agrees to include a 24x7 S1 escalation in a 12mo deal at 15% seat discount, require a minimum 12mo committed spend floor (eg. $250k ARR) to avoid churn exposure.

Tom — FYI, this is internal commentary. Jordan, happy to jump on a quick call to model the TCV and margin impact.

Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

> Tom / Sara — attached is the proposal packet (sla_uplift_options.pdf) with three options and worked examples. Summary below:
> ...

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <tom.m@brightgrid.ai>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: internal: BrightGrid — pricing anchor and concession guardrails

Team — ran the TCV scenarios and attached the modeling (bg_modeling.csv). High level:
- Plus 12mo at 10% seat discount = estimated ARR $1.1M with blended gross margin ~46% (tokens + seats).
- If we tier to 15% seat discount with 12mo commit, margin drops to ~39% but still above threshold if escalation add-on remains opt-in.
- 24mo commit with 18% seat discount yields ARR $2.0M and margin ~43% (we amortize onboarding).

Concession suggestion to close: offer 15% seat discount for 12mo if BrightGrid signs a minimum $300k committed spend in first 6 months; include a one-time onboarding fee to preserve initial gross. Escalation: include 24x7 S1 for the first 3 months, then convert to paid add-on (or include permanently at Enterprise).

I can sign off on the 15% concession if legal approves the SLA credit cap as written (30% monthly cap) and we add a requirement for monthly usage reporting + quarterly review.

— Aditya
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: bg_modeling.csv (csv stub)

From: Tom Miller <tom.m@brightgrid.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara@brightgrid.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA uplift & seat discount — proposal packet

Jordan — thanks for the clear options and to your team for the modeling. BrightGrid is prepared to move forward with Option B (Plus) on a 12-month term with the following conditions: 
- 15% seat discount at contract signature (currently 50 seats, potential to scale to 100 within 12 months)
- Include 24x7 S1 escalation for the first 6 months (we'll review after Q1)
- SLA credits as you proposed but we would like a guaranteed response SLA window documented for S2 incidents as well (4 business hours)
- Add DocuSign link for signature and the HubSpot deal ID in the agreement

If you can send a DocuSign with those bullets and the SLA amendment, we can get legal to review quickly. Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to piloting Redwood for our production use.

Tom Miller
Head of Platform
BrightGrid
